units.title: Hello
units.topic: Daily life: interaction, polite behaviour (交往)
notes: Chinese has two words for "you": 你 nǐ, for friends and people your own age, and 您 nín, a polite "you" for elders, teachers and people you want to show respect to. 您好 is a respectful hello.
In class, students greet their teacher together with 老师好! ("hello, teacher"). Among friends a greeting is often simply the other person's name.

dialogue.en: Sorry, I'm not a student, I'm a teacher.
dialogue.text: 对不起，我不是学生，我是老师。

units.title: About me
units.topic: Basic information: personal information (个人信息)
notes: In a Chinese name the family name comes first. In 王丽 Wáng Lì, 王 is the family name and 丽 the given name. Most family names are a single character.
People are often addressed by family name and title, like 李老师 ("Teacher Li"), rather than by their given name.
你几岁？ expects a small number, so it is how you ask a child's age. With adults, 你多大？ is more usual, and elders are asked more politely still.

dialogue.en: Yes, she's our teacher. She's Teacher Li.
dialogue.text: 是，她是我们老师，她叫李老师。

dialogue.en: Nice to meet you too! Where are you from?
dialogue.text: 我也很高兴！你是哪国人？
我是英国人。你是中国人吗？

dialogue.en: Teacher Li, is this your child?
dialogue.text: 李老师，这是您的孩子吗？

dialogue.en: How old are you, little one?
He's little. And you? How old are you this year?
dialogue.text: 他很小。你呢？你今年多大？

builds.en: How old are you? (to a child)

units.title: Numbers and dates
units.topic: Basic information: event information (事件信息)
notes: Before a measure word, "two" is 两 liǎng, not 二 èr: 两个人, two people. 二 is for counting and for numbers like 十二.
Dates run from big to small: year, month, day. Years are read digit by digit (二零二六年), and in speech the day of the month is 号.

dialogue.en: How many of you are there?
One, two, three, four. There are four of us.
He's seven. His friend is nine.

builds.en: How many of you are there?

dialogue.en: Today is Saturday, tomorrow is Sunday.
dialogue.text: 今天星期六，明天星期天。

dialogue.en: Last year was 2025, next year is 2027.
dialogue.text: 去年是二零二五年，明年是二零二七年。

units.title: Family
units.topic: Basic information: personal information, family and friends (个人信息)
notes: Chinese names older and younger siblings differently: 哥哥 and 姐姐 are older brother and sister, 弟弟 and 妹妹 younger ones.
个 is the everyday measure word, but animals take 只: 一只猫, a cat.

dialogue.en: How many people are in your family?
Dad, Mum, my older brother, my younger sister and me.
dialogue.text: 爸爸，妈妈，哥哥，妹妹和我。

dialogue.en: Do you have an older sister?
I don't have an older sister. And you?
I have a younger brother, and no older brother.
dialogue.text: 我有一个弟弟，没有哥哥。

dialogue.en: How old is your younger brother?

builds.en: There are five people in my family.
I don't have an older sister.
Do you have a younger brother?

dialogue.en: Yes. This is my son, and that's my daughter.
dialogue.text: 是。这是我的儿子，那是我的女儿。

dialogue.en: Does your son have a girlfriend?
He does, he loves her very much.
And your daughter? Does she have a boyfriend?
dialogue.text: 你的女儿呢？她有男朋友吗？

dialogue.en: She's eight! She loves our cat.
dialogue.text: 她八岁！她爱我们家的猫。

dialogue.en: We have a dog. It's called Dahei.
dialogue.text: 我家有一只狗，它叫大黑。

units.title: Eating
units.topic: Daily life: food and drink (饮食)
notes: Rice (米饭) is the everyday staple in the south of China; noodles (面条儿) and steamed buns (包子) more so in the north.
The 儿 at the end of 面条儿 is erhua, typical of Beijing speech; many speakers simply say 面条.

dialogue.en: What would you like to eat?
What would you like to drink? Tea?
No, I don't drink tea. I'll have water.
I'll have milk. I'm really hungry!

builds.en: What would you like to drink?

dialogue.en: What do you have for breakfast?
I have eggs and bread, and drink milk.
dialogue.text: 我吃鸡蛋和面包，喝牛奶。

dialogue.en: I have steamed buns. They're delicious!
dialogue.text: 我早饭吃包子。包子很好吃！

dialogue.en: Rice and vegetables. For dinner I have noodles.
dialogue.text: 米饭和菜。晚饭我吃面条儿。

builds.en: I have steamed buns for breakfast.

units.title: Shopping
notes: Prices are in 元 yuán on labels, but in speech people say 块 kuài: 五块 is five yuan.
太…了 means "too…": 太贵了, too expensive. The 了 marks it as a reaction to how things are.

dialogue.en: Hello! How much are the apples?
It's not expensive, it's cheap! How many would you like?
I'll take two. What else do you sell?
I also sell milk and bread.
You look pretty in this one.
What about that one? That one's nice too.
Things in this shop are expensive.
Things at the supermarket are cheap.

builds.en: Things at the supermarket are cheap.

units.title: Getting around
notes: To ask a stranger anything, start with 请问, "may I ask": it is the polite way in.
坐 means "to sit", and it is also how you take a vehicle: 坐出租车, 坐火车, 坐飞机.

dialogue.en: How are you getting to Shanghai tomorrow?
He doesn't drive. We take taxis.
dialogue.text: 他不开车。我们坐出租车。

dialogue.en: Excuse me, is this a taxi?
Yes, this is my car. Please, have a seat!
We're going to the supermarket, is that all right?

units.title: Weather and time
units.topic: Basic information: environment, weather (环境信息)
notes: 有点儿 means "a bit", and usually a bit too much of something unwelcome: 有点儿冷, a bit cold.
Clock times: 点 is o'clock, 分 minutes and 半 half past: 九点半 is half past nine.

dialogue.en: A bit cold. It's been really hot these last few days!
I don't like rain. I like snow!
I like snow too, it's beautiful.
What time do you have breakfast?
You're early! I eat at ten past eight.
Are you at home in the morning?
In the morning, yes; at noon and in the afternoon, no.
dialogue.text: 上午在家，中午和下午不在。

dialogue.en: In the evening I'm at home.

builds.en: Are you at home in the morning?

units.title: School
units.topic: Education: study and campus life (学习情况, 校园生活)
notes: 汉语 and 中文 both mean Chinese. 汉语 is the usual word for the language you study; 中文 is common for written Chinese, as in 中文书, a Chinese book.
Lessons begin with 上课 and end with 下课. Starting and finishing work are 上班 and 下班: 上 for going to, 下 for leaving.

dialogue.en: I study Chinese at a school in Beijing.
dialogue.text: 我在北京的一个学校学习汉语。

dialogue.en: What time do your classes start?
They start at eight and finish at twelve.
Yes, it's my Chinese book. I have no classes this afternoon.
dialogue.text: 是，这是我的中文书。今天下午没有课。

dialogue.en: Yes, we're university students. Our university is big. My younger sister is at secondary school.
dialogue.text: 是，我们是大学生。我们的大学很大。我妹妹是中学生。

dialogue.en: My younger brother is at primary school. He's seven and started school this year.
dialogue.text: 我弟弟是小学生。他七岁，今年上学。

dialogue.en: His primary school is over there, and my secondary school was there too.
dialogue.text: 他的小学在那儿，我的中学也在那儿。

dialogue.en: Characters. Does this one look right?
dialogue.text: 我写汉字。这个字好看吗？

builds.en: My younger brother is at primary school.

units.title: Work
units.topic: Work: work and occupations (工作情况, 职业)
notes: 先生 and 女士 are polite titles after a family name: 王先生, Mr Wang; 李女士, Ms Li.
Answering the phone, people say 喂, "hello?", often with a rising tone.

dialogue.en: Very. I start at eight and finish at seven in the evening.
dialogue.text: 很忙。我八点上班，晚上七点下班。

dialogue.en: Are Mr Wang and Ms Li at your company too?
dialogue.text: 王先生和李女士也在你们公司吗？

dialogue.en: Yes. They have something on today, so they're not at work.
dialogue.text: 是。他们今天有事，不上班。

dialogue.en: Hi, it's David. Can you talk now?
dialogue.text: 喂，我是大卫。你现在可以说话吗？

dialogue.en: I'd like to ask you something.
I don't know. Call Xiaoming and ask; he knows.
dialogue.text: 我不知道。你打电话问小明，他知道。

dialogue.en: Right! I've got his mobile number. Thanks!
dialogue.text: 对！他的手机我知道。谢谢！

builds.en: I'd like to ask a question.

units.title: Feeling ill
notes: 没事 means "it's nothing": 我没事, I'm fine. It is one of the most common reassurances in Chinese.
When someone is ill, the usual advice is to drink plenty of water and rest: 多喝水, 多休息.

dialogue.en: You should go to the hospital and see a doctor.
It's nothing, not a serious illness.
You need to rest and drink plenty of water.
Don't go to work; you need to sleep.

dialogue.text: 我吃一点儿东西，可以吗？

dialogue.en: Yes. And go to bed a bit early.
What time do you get up?
I get up late, at nine!
I sleep eight hours a day.
Not in the daytime; in the evening I do.
I'm going to rest for a bit, ten minutes.

builds.en: What time do you get up?

units.title: Free time
notes: 会 and 能 both mean "can". 会 is for skills you have learned (我会唱歌, I can sing); 能 is for being able to, or being allowed to.
吧 at the end of a sentence turns it into a suggestion: 我们去书店吧!, let's go to the bookshop!

dialogue.en: What are you doing on Sunday?
I'm going to the cinema to see a film.
I'll be at home watching TV and listening to music.
Very much. My younger sister sings beautifully.
dialogue.text: 很喜欢。我妹妹唱歌很好听。

dialogue.en: Where do you go to have fun?
We go round to Xiaoming's; it's great fun!
dialogue.text: 我们去小明家玩，很好玩儿！

builds.en: She listens to music at home.

dialogue.en: A little. I can read characters too.
dialogue.text: 会一点儿。我也能读汉字。

dialogue.en: What do you think of Chinese?
I think Chinese is great fun!
dialogue.text: 我觉得汉语非常好玩儿！

dialogue.en: Let's go to the bookshop on Sunday!
Great! I love reading. Can you come?
dialogue.text: 好！我喜欢读书。你能去吗？

dialogue.en: Yes! I don't want to stay home on the computer.

units.title: Things around me
notes: Measure words sort nouns: 本 for books (三本书), 件 for clothes, and 个 for most other things.
这些 and 那些, "these" and "those", make a plural without changing the noun: 这些书, these books.

dialogue.en: Yes. This is my desk and chair.
dialogue.text: 是。这是我的桌子和椅子。

dialogue.en: These are mine; those are my younger sister's.
dialogue.text: 这些是我的，那些是我妹妹的。

dialogue.en: How many Chinese books do you have?
This one's mine. Let's go and buy some cups!
dialogue.text: 这个是我的。我们去买些杯子吧！

dialogue.en: Here it is! There you go.
Thanks! This phone cost two thousand yuan.
That's so expensive! Mine was eight hundred.
dialogue.text: 太贵了！我的手机八百块。

dialogue.en: I have some money, and I give half to my mum.
dialogue.text: 我有一些钱，我给妈妈一半。

dialogue.en: Some classmates have very little money.
Some things are cheap, and some are expensive.
dialogue.text: 有些东西很便宜，有些很贵。

builds.en: My phone was eight hundred yuan.
I give half to my mum.

units.title: Here and there
units.topic: Basic information: places and directions (事件信息, 环境信息)
notes: 里 after a noun means "inside": 家里, at home; 书店里, in the bookshop. 上 and 下 work the same way for on and under: 桌子上, on the table.
住在 says where you live: 我住在北京.

dialogue.en: I'm at home. Is it cold out?
Very! There are lots of foreigners here.
dialogue.text: 很冷！这里有很多外国人。

dialogue.en: What about there? Is the supermarket on this side?
Not this side; it's on that side, next to the bookshop.
dialogue.text: 不在这边，在那边，书店边上。

builds.en: The book is on the table.
The cat is under the chair.

dialogue.en: How many people are in your family?
Four. There's a supermarket in front of our home.
dialogue.text: 四口人。我家前边有一个超市。

dialogue.en: Yes, he's switching on his computer.
Can you hear that? They're singing.
dialogue.text: 你听见了吗？她们在唱歌。

dialogue.en: I can! Where are our cats?

builds.en: How many people are in your family?

units.title: Chinese food
notes: Dumplings (饺子) are a family favourite across northern China, eaten above all at Spring Festival; families often make them together.
饭店 can mean a restaurant or a hotel; in everyday talk it usually means a restaurant.

dialogue.en: I can't cook. Let's go to a restaurant for dumplings!
dialogue.text: 我不会做饭。我们去饭店吃饺子吧！

dialogue.en: Great! The dumplings here are really good; my classmates all love them.
dialogue.text: 好！这个店的饺子非常好吃，我的男同学和女同学都喜欢。

dialogue.en: This is my first dumpling ever! It's so good!
dialogue.text: 这是我第一个饺子！真好吃！

builds.en: Let's go to a restaurant for dumplings!

builds.text: 这个店的饺子非常好吃。
builds.en: The dumplings here are really good.
